title: P02 dual tracers admit unchanged transit-age distributions at 5 percent tolerance in 2013 and 2022
abstract: We test whether North Pacific repeat-section tracers require a change in transit-age distribution. We use P02 CFC-12 and SF6 at 28-32 N on sigma0 26.3-26.7. An exact convex-hull method tests every nonnegative age mixture under linearly interpolated northern atmospheric histories, fixed sample-based solubility normalization and 100 percent source saturation. All 15 main regional density means admit one unchanged distribution for 2013 and 2022 within 5 percent error per tracer observation. Central-Pacific minimum errors are 0.64-2.19 percent; adding 2004 CFC-12 gives 0.85-2.21 percent. Positive witnesses and independent dual bounds verify all 30 fixed-saturation fits. Three-degree bins retain small central errors, but strict interpolation removes central coverage. These tracer means therefore do not require changed transport at the tested tolerance, despite earlier oxygen-loss evidence. They also do not establish steady transport. Source saturation, source solubility, sampling, interpolation, regional averaging and unconstrained spectrum shapes limit process inference. Code, hashes, aggregate evidence and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Minimum relative tracer error for one unchanged age distribution. Shading shows conditional spatial block intervals. Central Pacific fits remain small when 2004 CFC-12 is added.
